9 out-of-order times, G = 47 → 1..130 220..260 540..540 · one arrival joins 2 runs · 6 run(s) withdrawn
2 // primitive: ARRIVALS — the times, in the order they arrive. NOT sorted.
4 // primitive: G = 47 — two times belong to the same run if they are no further apart.
5 // primitive: run(start, end) — one run, written start..end. A single time is start==end.
7 // primitive: startOf(r) / endOf(r) — the two ends of a run.
9 // primitive: minOf(xs) / maxOf(xs) — the smallest and largest of a list.
13 // primitive: last(runs) — the final run in a list.
15 // primitive: setEnd(r, t) — move a run's end to t.
17 // primitive: starts(runs) / ends(runs) — the two ends of each run, as lists.
19 // primitive: contains(runs, r) — is that exact run still in the list?
21 // primitive: byStart(runs) — the runs ordered by where they begin.
23 // primitive: without(runs, some) — the runs that are not in `some`.
27 // "Door entries give one person's times. A VISIT is a run of entries with no gap
28 // longer than G. The times arrive OUT OF ORDER, and keep arriving. Report the
31 // function: sweep(times) — the batch answer: sort, then walk. Only correct if every
46 // function: touching(runs, t) — every run this time could join: one whose end is within
47 // G after t, or whose start is within G before it. There may be SEVERAL.
60 // function: absorb(runs, t) — replace every touched run, and the new time, with ONE run
61 // spanning all of them. This is where a late time joins two visits.
72 // function: withdrawn(before, after) — runs the consumer was shown that no longer exist.
73 // Nothing can un-send a report, so these have to be revisable.
83 // function: main() — the batch answer, then the same thing one arrival at a time.
95 // 6 run(s) had to be withdrawn along the way
Step 3/0 — so: which runs does one new time touch?

A time joins a run if it is within G of either end — so the test is two comparisons against a run's start and end, not against its members. With no runs yet, nothing is touched and the time becomes a run
